name: Cerebrofacial Arteriovenous Metameric Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Cerebrofacial Arteriovenous Metameric Syndrome Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Presence of arteriovenous malformations involving craniofacial structures in a metameric distribution
Intracranial arteriovenous malformations or fistulas corresponding to the same metameric segment
Radiological evidence (MRI, angiography) demonstrating cerebrofacial vascular malformations in a segmental pattern
Exclusion of other syndromes with overlapping vascular malformations such as Sturge-Weber syndrome or hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of craniofacial and intracranial arteriovenous malformations in a metameric distribution confirmed by imaging
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on clinical and radiological correlation; genetic testing is not definitive.

pathognomonic.notes: Typically unilateral and following metameric distribution
searchTerms: localized abnormal blood vessel growth on face

pathognomonic.notes: Localized to the same metameric segment as facial lesions
Distinct segmental pattern involving both brain and face
searchTerms: metameric pattern of blood vessel malformations

common.symptomName: Seizures secondary to intracranial vascular malformations
common.notes: Often focal seizures related to lesion location
searchTerms: seizures caused by brain vessel malformations
headache linked to blood vessel malformations

common.symptomName: Facial swelling or soft tissue hypertrophy
common.notes: Due to vascular malformation and associated tissue changes

occasional.symptomName: Epistaxis related to nasal vascular malformations
searchTerms: nosebleeds from nasal blood vessel issues
epistaxis due to nasal vascular malformations

occasional.symptomName: Visual disturbances from orbital vascular involvement
searchTerms: vision problems from eye socket vessels
orbital vascular involvement causing visual issues

occasional.symptomName: Cognitive impairment secondary to cerebral involvement
searchTerms: cognitive impairment due to brain issues

occasional.notes: Due to vascular anomalies near auditory structures

searchTerms: intracranial hemorrhage due to abnormal vessels

rare.symptomName: High-output cardiac failure due to large arteriovenous shunts
searchTerms: heart failure from large blood vessel shunts
heart overload due to AV shunts
brain fluid buildup from vein blockage
fluid accumulation due to venous outflow problems

laboratory: No specific laboratory abnormalities; routine blood tests typically normal
imaging: MRI and MR angiography showing segmental cerebrofacial arteriovenous malformations
Digital subtraction angiography demonstrating arteriovenous shunting in metameric distribution
CT scan may show calcifications or hemorrhage
genetic: No consistent genetic mutation identified; sporadic cases predominate
other: Clinical examination revealing segmental vascular skin lesions and facial asymmetry

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of facial port-wine stain not following metameric distribution
Leptomeningeal angiomas rather than arteriovenous malformations
Family history of autosomal dominant inheritance
Frequent epistaxis and visceral arteriovenous malformations

redFlags: Sudden onset neurological deficits indicating hemorrhage
